audit.whatIsWrong: Four rows contradicted the already-audited mirror, and two of them contradicted this page's own prose: the chart gave Darius First item and 2+ items while whys[5], whys[6], spikes[2], spikes[3] and 'late' all say Swain out-poke and out-sustains him at exactly those stages.
audit.why: The mirror (darius__swain) set Level 3 to Darius, Level 6 to Swain, First item to Skill and 2+ items to Swain. Mirrors must agree, and here the mirror also matches our own text.
audit.corrected: Row 2 to Darius, row 4 to Swain, row 5 to Skill, row 6 to Swain, proposed as matched full/content pairs, with ratings adjusted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both whys[3] and 'mid' state Apprehend's cooldown as '24-second base'. It is 26/23.5/21/18.5/16s — 26s at rank 1. The entire mid-game plan is keyed to that clock.
audit.why: Two seconds early into a 535-range pull is the difference between the punish window and the all-in he wants.
audit.corrected: 26s written into whys[3], mid, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three interactions were absent from the trading text. Decimate heals him off champions hit by the blade, so chip poke without Grievous Wounds is refunded. Noxian Guillotine is true damage, so the MR the itemisation implies does nothing to the execute. Crippling Strike is an auto-attack reset, so the burst tell is the wind-up rather than the pull.
audit.why: Riot's text: Q 'Darius heals based on enemy champions ... hit by the blade'; R 'dealing true damage'; W carries the autoReset flag.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[0].d names Decimate's healing, dontsFull[1].d names the Crippling Strike reset, dontsFull[2].d states the true damage, and mid now places Grievous Wounds before the level-6 window.

edits.before: Apprehend's 24-second base cooldown is the lane's clock — track it precisely and give nothing when it is up; commit the full poke pattern only in its window, banking small percentage leads.
edits.after: Apprehend is 26s at rank 1 and it is the lane's clock — give nothing while it is up, commit the full poke pattern inside its window, and bank small percentage leads every cycle.

edits.before: From level 4 onward the lane becomes a cooldown war: Apprehend on a 24-second base cooldown is his only reliable way into you, and you win every window where it is down. Watch the pull animation, note the timestamp when it whiffs or you dodge it, and commit your full W-slow into E-root into Q-burst pattern inside that window. Keep the wave on your side of the river so he must walk into your W range to last-hit — this forces the Apprehend under your watch rather than his. Level 6 is your inflection point: the moment Demonic Ascension is live, his all-in becomes your kill setup. He wants to bleed you to execute threshold, you want to drain back above it during his Decimate animation, stack another fragment, and recast Demonflare if he pops Ghost to chase.
edits.after: From level 4 onward the lane becomes a cooldown war: Apprehend is 26 seconds at rank 1 and his only reliable way into you, so you win every window where it is down. Watch the pull animation, note the timestamp when it whiffs or you dodge it, and commit your full W-slow into E-root into Q-burst pattern inside that window. Keep the wave on your side of the river so he must walk into your W range to last-hit — that forces the Apprehend under your watch rather than his. Have Grievous Wounds by now, because Decimate's blade heals him off every trade you take. Level 6 is your inflection point: the moment Demonic Ascension is live his all-in becomes your kill setup — drain back above the execute threshold during his Decimate animation and recast Demonflare if he Ghosts in to chase.
